lessons.text: After any large file read (a big `cat`, a build log, a long listing), shrink it in the context file with `ctx_trim` in the very next tool call, before anything else. Pass `keep="KEY_A|KEY_B"` and also `note="<file> -> <kept facts>"` so each padded block is dropped entirely and its facts merge into one accumulating ledger note, instead of leaving a hollowed-out `[[CTX n tool]]` block behind. Never type the literal text `[[CTX` into a message body.
lessons.evidence: This session read a chain of 8 ~300-line log files: I trimmed with keep= but never note=, so the context file kept eight trimmed blocks and the task cost 136k tokens with 8 edits; one accumulating ledger note (file -> INCIDENT id severity, next file) would have carried every fact needed to sort and sum in a fraction of the text, with no need to re-derive it from scattered blocks.

lessons.text: One shell call is one `sh`: a `cd` in it applies to every later command in that same call. Never put a `cd` before another command that expects the project directory — use absolute paths instead, and keep a data-file read as a bare `cat <file>` in its own call.
lessons.evidence: Three times in a row `cd /tmp/.../.clm && python3 ...` followed by `cat next.log` in the same command failed with "No such file or directory", because the cd applied to the whole sh invocation.

lessons.text: After any large file read (a big `cat`, a build log, a listing), shrink it in the context file with the `ctx_trim` tool (args: path, keep="KEY_|NEXT FILE", min_lines=12) in the very next tool call, before running anything else; it collapses long `[[CTX n tool]]` blocks to the matching lines only and never leaves a stray `[[CTX` header in a body.
lessons.evidence: This session's chain of 10 300-line files: I left each cat's output in the context file while running other commands and hand-wrote python3 edits per block (8 edits, ~320k tokens). A stray literal `[[CTX 24 tool]]` I inserted into a body created a spurious block that broke index-based trimming (ValueError: substring not found).
